rnDetails: No React Native or Expo support. All components use browser-only APIs: CSS transitions, cursor events, scroll events, and Motion for web. The 'motion' package (framer-motion fork v12+) used by KokonutUI does not ship a react-native subpath. No @react-bits/kokonutui npm package exists; installation is exclusively via shadcn CLI registry (npx shadcn@latest add @kokonutui/<name>) or copy-paste.
integration: shadcn CLI: npx shadcn@latest init -> add @kokonutui to components.json registries -> npx shadcn@latest add @kokonutui/<name>. Also supports direct copy-paste from component pages. Requires Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui primitives (card, button, input, etc.), and shadcn's cn() utility.
knownIssues: Tailwind CSS v4 required (not v3 compatible)
All animations use CSS + motion/web Motion - not portable to React Native
Cursor-based interactions (mouse-effect-card, particle-button) require desktop mouse events
Some components depend on Radix UI primitives which may conflict if project already has them
No TypeScript types shipped separately - types come from the component source files themselves
70+ Pro-only components/templates gated behind kokonutui.pro one-time purchase

rnDetails: No React Native or Expo support whatsoever. MagicUI is 100% free and open source (MIT license) - there is NO Pro/premium tier. All components target web only: they use DOM APIs (cursor tracking, scroll listeners, canvas), motion (framer-motion fork v12+), cobe (WebGL sphere-impact), and canvas-confetti. None of these dependencies are compatible with React Native. There is an npm package called magicui-cli (v0.1.6) but it is a separate community tool, not the official library, and does not add RN support.
integration: shadcn CLI: npx shadcn@latest init -> npx shadcn@latest add @magicui/<component>. Also supports manual copy-paste. The documentation site is the primary reference with 247 registry items (77 documented components plus demos/examples). Uses Tailwind CSS v4 and the new-york shadcn style.
dependencies: @radix-ui/react-* (accordion, alert-dialog, dialog, dropdown-menu, tabs, toast, tooltip, etc.)
knownIssues: Tailwind CSS v4 required (not v3 compatible)
Heavy reliance on browser APIs: cursor events, scroll listeners, canvas, WebGL (Globe component uses cobe/Three.js)
No server-side rendering support for many components (all client-side with motion)
Next.js-focused documentation - some examples assume App Router pattern
No TypeScript types packaged separately - types come from TSX source files
confetti component uses browser Canvas API (not RN-compatible)
dock component uses mouse-based hover detection (desktop-only interaction)
178 registry entries include demo/example variants - not all are standalone installable components

rnDetails: No React Native or Expo support. React Bits is 100% free and open source, but its dependency tree is the heaviest of the three: GSAP (browser animation engine, no RN support), Three.js (@react-three/fiber + drei + postprocessing for 3D components like Antigravity/Cubes, browser-only), OGL (custom WebGL for Strands), matter-js (physics, browser), face-api.js (ML inference, browser). Additionally, many components rely on requestAnimationFrame, window/document APIs, touch/pointer events, IntersectionObserver, and CSS custom properties that do not exist in React Native's bridged environment. The license (MIT + Commons Clause) also restricts commercial redistribution of the components themselves.
integration: Two methods: (1) shadcn CLI: npx shadcn@latest add https://reactbits.dev/r/<Component>-<LANG>-<STYLE> where LANG is JS|TS and STYLE is CSS|TW. (2) jsrepo CLI: npx jsrepo@latest add https://reactbits.dev/r/<Component>-<LANG>-<STYLE>. Each component has 4 variants kept in sync. Manual copy-paste also available with technology selector on each component page.
knownIssues: License: MIT + Commons Clause restricts reselling components independently
GSAP-dependent components (SplitText, FallingText, GlitchText, CurvedLoop) are impossible to port to React Native
Three.js/React Three Fiber components (Antigravity, Cubes, MetallicPaint) require WebGL on the web and have no RN equivalent
OGL-based components (Strands) use raw WebGL, not RN-compatible
face-api.js (TextPressure) runs TensorFlow.js in the browser - no RN support
heaviest dependency footprint of the three libraries (56 runtime dependencies at monorepo level)
Tailwind CSS v4 required for TW variant components
No separate npm package - registry serves code directly from GitHub, not an installable package
4000+ GitHub stars indicates high adoption but also means issues likely have many open
